content:
Last month we held a poll, and the overwhelming majority of 9to5Mac readers agreed that Apple should exit the advertising business.

Ads have landed in Apple Maps in the US and Canada, and I think it's every bit as obnoxious as you'd imagine…

Apple previewed way back in March that ads would appear in the Maps app at some point this summer. We finally got our first look at them yesterday, with Apple confirming that ads have been rolling out over the past few days, with all users in the US and Canada set to see them over the coming weeks.

  • Before search: Sponsored suggestions will appear below 'Featured Places' on the search page.
  • After search: Ads will appear next to relevant search results.

Apple says privacy is one of its priorities.

I absolutely believe that, but for two reasons I still find the whole thing tacky.

John Atkinson's top comment:

The only non-ad-revenue reason I can think of for adding ads to Apple Maps is that it might be used as an incentive to encourage more businesses to claim their business listings. Apple Maps has never caught up to Google Maps, and one of the long-standing reasons for that is that many businesses simply don't want to take the time to add themselves to the map, or update their information to prevent it from going stale. In North America, this isn't a huge issue because of high iPhone penetration, but internationally it absolutely is.

In theory, ads could serve as an incentive for businesses to upload their info, since they could then advertise within the same app (or rather, in order to advertise, their marketing teams would have to fill out all the info). But I don't think that's why Apple is doing this? Definitely not — obviously it's to make more money — but there is at least a side benefit of hopefully improving map data quality.

First, while Apple won't serve you personalized ads via any form of tracking, virtually every other app and website does. People will naturally assume the iPhone maker does too — however unfair that perception may be — and that damages Apple's reputation for protecting user privacy.

Second, it's just tacky. In the app and web publishing ecosystem, ads are a necessary evil: it's precisely because of them that free apps or websites can keep running. But Apple absolutely doesn't need ad revenue to pay the rent: its premium hardware pricing is already high enough. Advertising is fundamentally at odds with the Apple brand.

I remember John Gruber once compared ads in Apple apps to those annoying 'Intel Inside' stickers on cheap Windows laptops. Of course we understand that cheap laptop makers need to chase every possible revenue source, but we never imagined Apple would slap the equivalent on a MacBook to cheapen the brand. So how can we accept ads in our own Apple devices' own apps?

My position hasn't changed: Apple simply shouldn't be in the advertising business.
